analysis: Examined ClusterServiceControl.swift (base vs head) and the test-group registration in ClusterConsoleCheck.swift. Changes in ClusterServiceControl.swift: (1) ensureControlResponder (head lines 108-131) now uses listenerChange(of:checked:\.controlCheck), listenerSelection(), listening.controlPort and listening.policy instead of cableMove/context.linkSelection/fixed ClusterSetupLinkExchange.controlPort. The control listener thus follows re-pairing as well as cable moves. The responder is still keyed by the pairing and accepts only lease commands (receiveLease at line 133 rejects non-lease ops; answer/receive closures throw). (2) ensureControl (head 175-200) now also drops the control node when node.localID != pairing.localMemberID, so a Mac re-paired under a new key of its own no longer keeps a stale leader claim. This tightens the lease/claim state relative to the pairing and I see no regression. The test change only registers a new group, listenersFollowThePairing, whose body is not in the supplied evidence. The model's mapping to the threat model is loose: this is local cluster-control code, nothing in it touches the consumer-data, attestation or App Attest paths, and no listed threat ID cleanly matches it, so there are no threat_ids to cite. Unverified: the implementations of listenerChange, listenerSelection, and the `listening` struct (including `policy` and a possibly non-fixed controlPort) are outside the supplied evidence. A reviewer with the full branch should check that listening.policy does not widen which peers/addresses the responder accepts, and that a dynamic port or policy cannot bind to unintended interfaces. The pairing-key authentication of the Responder is assumed unchanged. No finding is supportable from the visible diff, so the remaining question is about the unseen helper definitions.
